content:
For years, collectors have been devoted fans of Steve Jobs memorabilia, and a new item seems poised to generate tremendous interest. It is his eighth-grade science fair project, containing two demonstration circuits, accompanied by a warning note written by Jobs to his teacher.

The item had been kept at the Jobs family property in Los Altos, but is now one of over 200 lots in an Apple 50th anniversary auction...

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and RR Auctions is holding a two-part auction titled "Steve Jobs and the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction" to mark the milestone. In the first part, the first cheque ever written by the company sold for as much as $2.4 million.

The second part includes this science fair project.

The warning note appears to alert the teacher that the circuits could burn out if left running for too long. As of writing, online bids were still under $3,000, but that figure is almost certain to be surpassed.

The auction also features a fully functional early Apple 1 computer.

As well as an engineering prototype of an original iPod.
